# Didache Chapter 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_007_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 7

**1** Now concerning baptism, baptize in this way: having said all these things beforehand, baptize into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit in living water.

**2** But if you do not have living water, baptize into other water; and if you are not able in cold water, then in warm.

**3** But if you have neither, pour water on the head three times into the name of the Father and Son and Holy Spirit.

**4** But before the baptism, let the one baptizing and the one being baptized fast, and also any others who are able. But command the one being baptized to fast one or two days before.

---

*EMET notes: "Living water" (ὕδωρ ζῶν) = running water, as opposed to still water — a technical term in Jewish purification contexts (cf. Lev 14:5; Num 19:17). The preference order: running water → still water (cold preferred over warm) → pouring. This is the earliest Christian text specifying baptismal modes. "Into the name of" (εἰς τὸ ὄνομα) = into the person/authority of (a transfer of ownership/allegiance). The trinitarian formula matches Matt 28:19 exactly. The fasting requirement is the earliest evidence for pre-baptismal fasting as a liturgical practice.*
